Search this repository (breadth: very thorough) for the identity provider / third-party authentication abstraction layer. I need to find:

1. A package that defines an abstraction (interface/contract) for third-party identity providers (SSO, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, etc.)
2. The concrete protocol implementation(s) that ship with the project (e.g., an OAuth2 or OIDC implementation of that abstraction)

Look for keywords: idp, identity provider, OAuth, OIDC, OpenID, SAML, SSO, provider, authenticator, social login, third-party auth.

Search in directories like internal/, pkg/, plugin/, server/, etc.

Report exact package paths, interface names, and implementation struct names with file paths and line numbers.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

9	// deriveSSOUsername produces the local username for a new SSO-created user.
10	//
11	// The current policy is to use a standard UUID string directly. This keeps the
12	// username independent of IdP profile fields and avoids availability probes or
13	// retry loops around concurrent first-time logins.
14	func deriveSSOUsername() (string, error) {
15		username := util.GenUUID()
16		if err := validateWritableUsername(username); err != nil {
17			return "", errors.Wrap(err, "generated UUID did not satisfy username constraints")
18		}
19		return username, nil
20	}

77	func newMockServer(t *testing.T, code, accessToken string, userinfo []byte) *httptest.Server {
78		mux := http.NewServeMux()
79	
80		var rawIDToken string
81		mux.HandleFunc("/oauth2/token", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
82			require.Equal(t, http.MethodPost, r.Method)
83	
84			body, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
85			require.NoError(t, err)
86			vals, err := url.ParseQuery(string(body))
87			require.NoError(t, err)
88	
89			require.Equal(t, code, vals.Get("code"))
90			require.Equal(t, "authorization_code", vals.Get("grant_type"))
91	
92			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
93			err = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{
94				"access_token": accessToken,
95				"token_type":   "Bearer",
96				"expires_in":   3600,
97				"id_token":     rawIDToken,
98			})
99			require.NoError(t, err)
100		})
101		mux.HandleFunc("/oauth2/userinfo", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
102			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
103			_, err := w.Write(userinfo)
104			require.NoError(t, err)
105		})
106	
107		s := httptest.NewServer(mux)
108	
109		return s
110	}

1	package v1
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5	
6		"golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt"
7		"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
8		"google.golang.org/grpc/status"
9		"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"
10	
11		v1pb "github.com/usememos/memos/proto/gen/api/v1"
12		"github.com/usememos/memos/store"
13	)
14	
15	const (
16		unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError = "unmatched username and password"
17	)
18	
19	// GetCurrentUser returns the authenticated user's information.
20	// Validates the access token and returns user details.
21	//
22	// Authentication: Required (access token).
23	// Returns: User information.
24	func (s *APIV1Service) GetCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, _ *v1pb.GetCurrentUserRequest) (*v1pb.GetCurrentUserResponse, error) {
25		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
26		if err != nil {
27			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "failed to get current user: %v", err)
28		}
29		if user == nil {
30			// Clear auth cookies
31			if err := s.clearAuthCookies(ctx); err != nil {
32				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to clear auth cookies: %v", err)
33			}
34			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not found")
35		}
36	
37		return &v1pb.GetCurrentUserResponse{
38			User: convertUserFromStore(user, user),
39		}, nil
40	}
41	
42	// SignIn authenticates a user with credentials and returns tokens.
43	// On success, returns an access token and sets a refresh token cookie.
44	//
45	// Supports two authentication methods:
46	// 1. Password-based authentication (username + password).
47	// 2. SSO authentication (OAuth2 authorization code).
48	//
49	// Authentication: Not required (public endpoint).
50	// Returns: User info, access token, and token expiry.
51	func (s *APIV1Service) SignIn(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.SignInRequest) (*v1pb.SignInResponse, error) {
52		var existingUser *store.User
53	
54		// Authentication Method 1: Password-based authentication
55		if passwordCredentials := request.GetPasswordCredentials(); passwordCredentials != nil {
56			user, err := s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{
57				Username: &passwordCredentials.Username,
58			})
59			if err != nil {
60				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user, error: %v", err)
61			}
62			if user == nil {
63				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError)
64			}
65			// Compare the stored hashed password, with the hashed version of the password that was received.
66			if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.PasswordHash), []byte(passwordCredentials.Password)); err != nil {
67				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, unmatchedUsernameAndPasswordError)
68			}
69			instanceGeneralSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceGeneralSetting(ctx)
70			if err != nil {
71				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get instance general setting, error: %v", err)
72			}
73			// Check if the password auth in is allowed.
74			if instanceGeneralSetting.DisallowPasswordAuth && user.Role == store.RoleUser {
75				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "password signin is not allowed")
76			}
77			existingUser = user
78		} else if ssoCredentials := request.GetSsoCredentials(); ssoCredentials != nil {
79			// Authentication Method 2: SSO (OAuth2) authentication
80			identityProvider, userInfo, err := s.resolveSSOIdentity(ctx, ssoCredentials.IdpName, ssoCredentials.Code, ssoCredentials.RedirectUri, ssoCredentials.CodeVerifier)
81			if err != nil {
82				return nil, err
83			}
84			user, err := s.resolveSSOUser(ctx, nil, identityProvider, userInfo)
85			if err != nil {
86				return nil, err
87			}
88			existingUser = user
89		}
90	
91		if existingUser == nil {
92			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid credentials")
93		}
94		if existingUser.RowStatus == store.Archived {
95			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "user has been archived with username %s", existingUser.Username)
96		}
97	
98		accessToken, accessExpiresAt, err := s.doSignIn(ctx, existingUser)
99		if err != nil {
100			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to sign in: %v", err)
101		}
102	
103		return &v1pb.SignInResponse{
104			User:                 convertUserFromStore(existingUser, existingUser),
105			AccessToken:          accessToken,
106			AccessTokenExpiresAt: timestamppb.New(accessExpiresAt),
107		}, nil
108	}
109	
110	// resolveSSOUser resolves a local user from an external-identity subject, creating the
111	// linkage record (and a new local user if necessary) when first login is allowed.
112	//
113	// Lookup goes through the user_identity table so that userInfo.Identifier is never used
114	// as the local username key. On the miss path, a local user is created with a
115	// UUID-based local username (see deriveSSOUsername) and the (provider, extern_uid)
116	// linkage is inserted in the same flow. When currentUser is provided by a caller
117	// outside AuthService.SignIn, the lookup miss path binds the external identity to
118	// that existing user instead. If the linkage insert loses a race on the unique
119	// (provider, extern_uid) constraint, the winning linkage's user is loaded and
120	// checked against the current user.

---

## Identity Provider / Third-Party Authentication Abstraction Layer

This project (usememos/memos) has a well-structured identity provider abstraction organized across three layers: a core abstraction package, a concrete OAuth2 implementation, and persistence/API glue.

---

### 1. Core Abstraction Package

**Package path:** `internal/idp`
**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go`

This is a minimal abstraction that defines the universal user-info return type shared by all identity provider implementations:

```go
package idp

type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
    Identifier  string
    DisplayName string
    Email       string
    AvatarURL   string
}
```

- **Struct name:** `IdentityProviderUserInfo` (line 3)
- This struct is the contract that every concrete identity provider implementation must produce. Any protocol-specific implementation (OAuth2, OIDC, SAML, etc.) receives protocol-specific tokens/responses and normalizes them into this common struct.

There is no Go `interface` keyword used here -- the abstraction is structural rather than behavioral. The protocol implementations are expected to provide methods `ExchangeToken(...)` and `UserInfo(...)` that ultimately return `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`. The dispatch to the correct implementation happens at the call site (see below).

---

### 2. Concrete OAuth2 Implementation

**Package path:** `internal/idp/oauth2`
**File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`

This is the sole protocol implementation that ships with the project. It implements OAuth2-based identity provider integration.

- **Struct name:** `IdentityProvider` (line 20)
- **Constructor:** `NewIdentityProvider(config *storepb.OAuth2Config) (*IdentityProvider, error)` (line 27)
- **Key methods:**
  - `ExchangeToken(ctx context.Context, redirectURL, code, codeVerifier string) (string, error)` (line 47) -- exchanges an authorization code for an access token, with PKCE support
  - `UserInfo(ctx context.Context, token string) (*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo, error)` (line 83) -- fetches user info from the provider's userinfo endpoint and maps it to the common `idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct using configurable field mappings

The configuration is driven by `storepb.OAuth2Config` (protobuf), which contains: `ClientId`, `ClientSecret`, `AuthUrl`, `TokenUrl`, `UserInfoUrl`, `Scopes`, and `FieldMapping` (with `Identifier`, `DisplayName`, `Email`, `AvatarUrl`).

**Test file:** `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2_test.go`

---

### 3. Protocol Dispatch (The "Switch" Point)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`
**Function:** `resolveSSOIdentity` (line 104)

This is where the abstraction is consumed. The function loads an `IdentityProvider` from the store, checks its `.Type`, and dispatches to the appropriate concrete implementation:

```go
if identityProvider.Type == storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2 {
    oauth2IdentityProvider, err := oauth2.NewIdentityProvider(identityProvider.Config.GetOauth2Config())
    // ... ExchangeToken, then UserInfo
}
```

Currently `OAUTH2` is the only supported type (the protobuf enum has `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0` and `OAUTH2 = 1`). Adding a new protocol (e.g., SAML) would require adding a new enum value and a new `else if` branch here.

---

### 4. Protobuf Data Model

**Proto source:** `store/idp.proto`
**Generated Go file:** `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go`

Key types:
- `IdentityProvider` message (line 70) -- top-level entity with `Id`, `Uid`, `Name`, `Type`, `IdentifierFilter`, `Config`
- `IdentityProvider_Type` enum (line 24) -- `TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0`, `OAUTH2 = 1`
- `IdentityProviderConfig` message (line 154) -- a `oneof config` that currently only holds `Oauth2Config`
- `OAuth2Config` message (line 288) -- full OAuth2 config with client credentials, endpoints, scopes, and field mappings
- `FieldMapping` message (line 220) -- maps provider claims to `Identifier`, `DisplayName`, `Email`, `AvatarUrl`

**API-level protobuf (gRPC service):**
- `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service.pb.go` -- API-facing IdentityProvider messages
- `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/api/v1/idp_service_grpc.pb.go` -- gRPC service definition
- `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/idp_service.connect.go` -- Connect RPC bindings

---

### 5. Persistence Layer

**Store abstraction (driver interface):**
`/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` -- the `Driver` interface (line 10) includes these identity-provider methods (lines 57-62):
- `CreateIdentityProvider(ctx, *IdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)`
- `ListIdentityProviders(ctx, *FindIdentityProvider) ([]*IdentityProvider, error)`
- `UpdateIdentityProvider(ctx, *UpdateIdentityProvider) (*IdentityProvider, error)`
- `DeleteIdentityProvider(ctx, *DeleteIdentityProvider) error`
- `ApplyAuthenticationConfigMutation(ctx, *AuthenticationConfigMutation) error`
- `IsRetryableAuthenticationMutationError(err error) bool`

And user-identity linkage methods (lines 83-85):
- `CreateUserIdentity(ctx, *UserIdentity) (*UserIdentity, error)`
- `ListUserIdentities(ctx, *FindUserIdentity) ([]*UserIdentity, error)`
- `DeleteUserIdentities(ctx, *DeleteUserIdentity) error`

**Store-level structs:** `/bench/home/work/store/idp.go`
- `IdentityProvider` struct (line 12) -- raw DB row model
- `FindIdentityProvider` struct (line 21)
- `UpdateIdentityProvider` / `UpdateIdentityProviderV1` structs (lines 26, 144)
- `DeleteIdentityProvider` struct (line 33)

**User identity linkage:** `/bench/home/work/store/user_identity.go`
- `UserIdentity` struct (line 8) -- links external identity subjects to local users with fields `ID`, `UserID`, `Provider`, `ExternUID`
- `FindUserIdentity` struct (line 17)
- `DeleteUserIdentity` struct (line 25)

**Database driver implementations (all three backends):**
- SQLite: `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/idp.go`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user_identity.go`
- PostgreSQL: `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/idp.go`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user_identity.go`
- MySQL: `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/idp.go`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user_identity.go`

---

### 6. Deployment Configuration (File-Backed IdPs)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/deployment_config.go`

Identity providers can also be loaded from JSON files on disk (from `/etc/secrets/`) with filenames matching `memos-idp-*.json`. These file-backed providers shadow database-stored ones when UIDs collide. This is handled by:
- `LoadDeploymentConfigurationDir()` (line 43)
- `validateDeploymentIdentityProvider()` (line 158)
- `IsIdentityProviderDeploymentConfigured()` (line 412)
- The `deploymentConfiguration` struct in `/bench/home/work/store/store.go` (line 32)

---

### 7. API / gRPC Service Layer

**IdP CRUD service:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go`
- `CreateIdentityProvider` (line 17)
- `ListIdentityProviders` (line 47)
- `GetIdentityProvider` (line 62)
- `UpdateIdentityProvider` (line 80)
- `DeleteIdentityProvider` (line 146)

**SSO sign-in flow:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`
- `SignIn` method (line 51) -- dispatches to password auth or SSO based on credentials type

**SSO resolution and user creation:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`
- `resolveSSOIdentity` (line 104) -- loads IdP, dispatches to OAuth2 implementation, applies identifier filter
- `resolveSSOUser` (line 19) -- finds or creates local user from SSO identity
- `getLinkedSSOUser` (line 150) -- looks up existing user-identity linkage
- `bindSSOIdentityToUser` (line 171) -- links an SSO identity to an existing user

**Linked identity management:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_identities.go`
- `ListLinkedIdentities` (line 14)
- `CreateLinkedIdentity` (line 39)
- `GetLinkedIdentity` (line 81)
- `DeleteLinkedIdentity` (line 106)

**SSO username generation:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go`
- `deriveSSOUsername()` (line 14) -- generates a UUID-based username for SSO-created users

**Auth configuration safety:** `/bench/home/work/store/auth_config.go`
- Ensures password auth cannot be disabled without at least one effective identity provider

---

### Summary

| Layer | Package | Key Types | File |
|-------|---------|-----------|------|
| Abstraction | `internal/idp` | `IdentityProviderUserInfo` | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go:3` |
| OAuth2 Implementation | `internal/idp/oauth2` | `IdentityProvider` (struct) | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20` |
| Protobuf Model | `proto/gen/store` | `IdentityProvider`, `IdentityProviderConfig`, `OAuth2Config`, `FieldMapping` | `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/idp.pb.go` |
| Store Driver Interface | `store` | `Driver` interface (IdP methods at lines 57-62) | `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go:10` |
| Store Structs | `store` | `IdentityProvider`, `UserIdentity` | `/bench/home/work/store/idp.go:12`, `/bench/home/work/store/user_identity.go:8` |
| API Service | `server/router/api/v1` | `APIV1Service` methods | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/idp_service.go`, `auth_service_sso.go` |

The project currently ships **only one** concrete protocol implementation: **OAuth2**. The type enum and config `oneof` are designed to be extended with additional protocols (e.g., SAML, OIDC-native) but no others exist in the codebase today.
